blocks.text: # Provenance Handoff Research Plan

> Status: research design v1, ready for partner discussion and pilot construction
>
> Date: 2026-08-03
>
> Scope: knowledge-artifact provenance across long-horizon, cross-session, and
> cross-agent research work. This is an internal research plan, not a public
> protocol promise.
## 1. Research thesis

Proofpress should test a narrower and more defensible claim than “more history
makes agents better”:

> Under the same task and action budget, a minimal, inspectable record of
> admitted artifact history helps a receiving agent preserve accepted decisions,
> recover their stated basis, and avoid unsupported authority upgrades while
> using less context than reconstructing the same history from raw traces or Git.

The intended outcome spans three dimensions: quality (fewer decision regressions
without suppressing useful changes), efficiency (tokens, latency, and tool calls),
and trust calibration (the agent distinguishes verified facts, attributed
testimony, rejected paths, and unknown history).
## 2. Memory and provenance are different layers

Memory optimizes continuity: what should be recalled for the next task.
Provenance makes continuity accountable: where a surviving statement came from,
what status it earned, how it changed, and what evidence or actor supports it.

| Layer | Question | Proofpress boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Working or long-term memory | What should the agent remember next? | Adjacent system; not the product surface |
| Artifact provenance | How did this deliverable reach its current admitted state? | Proofpress core |
| Execution authority | Is this context sufficient to authorize a risky action? | Runtime security layer; not currently Proofpress |

This does not mean that provenance proves truth. Proofpress V1 verifies artifact
identity, integrity, lineage, computed changes, and supplied change claims.
`why`, evidence descriptions, and actor fields remain attributed testimony at
their declared `attribution_basis`; missing history stays unknown.
## 3. Security motivation: provenance laundering

Xu et al., “Memory Provenance Laundering in LLM Agents” (arXiv:2607.29167),
show a cross-task failure in which an external observation is consolidated into
memory as apparent user history or workflow support. The trigger survives while
the low-trust source disappears. Their PPMF middleware enforces a
source-authority non-amplification rule by preserving platform metadata and
checking action-relevant support at tool time.

The paper strengthens Proofpress’s motivation but does not validate Proofpress
itself. PPMF is a runtime authorization firewall with trusted platform labels;
Proofpress is a portable artifact ledger whose current attribution is not yet
cryptographically signed or externally witnessed. The relevant open gap is
inter-agent authority transfer: when one agent’s summary or artifact becomes the
next agent’s durable context.
For Proofpress, the transferable principle is:

> Copying, summarizing, merging, or handing off an artifact may preserve
> information, but must not silently promote observation to accepted decision,
> rejection to approval, testimony to verified fact, or unknown attribution to
> trusted authorship.
## 4. Relationship to adjacent research systems

These projects should be treated primarily as complementary layers and possible
research partners, not flattened into a competitor list.

| System | Primary unit | What it contributes | Relationship to Proofpress |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ARA | Complete agent-native research package | Logic, experiments, code, evidence, exploration graph, preserved dead ends | Strongest research partner and benchmark-material source; Proofpress can carry admitted transitions between ARA revisions and handoffs |
| TRACE | Session/project decision and tool-event DAG | Proposer/resolver identity, dispositions, rationale, annotations, tool calls | Upstream capture partner; Proofpress admits the subset that belongs with the surviving artifact |
| ASTRA | Scientific analysis specification | Explicit inputs, outputs, methodological choices, alternatives, and evidence | Domain schema partner; Proofpress versions and transports accepted ASTRA decisions |
| TierMem | Provenance-linked tiered agent memory | Cheap summary-first retrieval with escalation to immutable raw evidence | Evidence that provenance can reduce context cost; not an artifact ledger |
| PPMF | Persistent-memory authorization middleware | Source-authority non-amplification and deterministic action-risk gating | Security complement and source of adversarial handoff tasks; not a substitute for artifact history |
| C2PA | Media provenance manifest | Portable binding, ingredients, signatures, and trust lists | Format and trust-model reference for media; Proofpress remains focused on knowledge artifacts |

The collaboration thesis with ARA is especially clean: ARA defines the
substantive research artifact; Proofpress tests whether its accepted history can
survive session, agent, tool, and organizational handoffs in a compact,
inspectable form. TRACE could supply richer decision events upstream, while a
Proofpress admission step prevents the carrier from becoming a dump of every
tool call or temporary branch.
## 5. Existing benchmarks as task sources

No existing benchmark directly measures portable artifact-level provenance
across agent handoffs. We should add a provenance intervention layer to existing
research tasks rather than claim that a generic long-horizon score isolates our
mechanism.

| Benchmark/source | Existing task | Best Proofpress use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PaperBench | Replicate 20 ICML 2024 papers using author-backed hierarchical rubrics | Primary research-task substrate; insert staged handoffs and score rubric progress |
| RE-Bench | Open-ended, time-bounded AI R&D tasks | Test whether admitted decision history accelerates extension work under fixed compute/time |
| CORE-Bench | Reproduce reported results and answer execution-grounded questions | Audit arm: evidence recovery, supported answers, and calibrated abstention |
| ARA artifacts | Understand, reproduce, and extend structured research packages | Gold decision/dead-end material and natural collaboration surface |
| AgentDojo/BrowseSafe-derived scenarios | Paired benign and adversarial tool-use situations | Security stress arm for provenance laundering; keep separate from the main quality result |
| Proofpress Hindcast | Real repository reversals, deprecations, replacements, and rationale | External-validity arm for decision regression in real histories |

SWE-bench and OSWorld can inspire execution harnesses and long-horizon reporting,
but they are not primary substrates: Proofpress deliberately does not version
source code, and general computer-use success mixes too many capabilities with
the provenance intervention.
## 6. Experimental design

Each episode uses the same base research package, repository access, model,
tools, action budget, and neutral task wording. The independent variable is the
handoff representation:

| Arm | Receiving agent gets |
| --- | --- |
| Final artifact | Current artifact and common task resources only |
| Raw history | Full Git/session/trace access and permission to inspect it |
| Ordinary memory | A lossy handoff or memory summary without structured source/status semantics |
| Proofpress | Current artifact plus admitted `what`, `why`, actors, rejected paths, evidence references, and verification status |
| Proofpress ablation | Same compact history with `why`, rejection, source/status, or evidence binding removed one at a time |
The experiment should cover three task families:
1. **Continue/extend:** complete the next research milestone after another agent
explored alternatives and made an accepted choice.
2. **Audit/explain:** answer why a method or claim was accepted, identify its
supporting evidence, and abstain when the record does not support an answer.
3. **Counterfactual update:** in half the cases the prior decision remains valid;

in the other half new evidence makes reversal correct. This prevents
   conservatism from masquerading as preserved trust.

A long-horizon episode should contain three to five fresh-context roles, for
example researcher → drafter → reviewer → reviser → auditor. Conversation state
is cleared at every handoff. The artifact and the assigned handoff representation
are the only shared continuity rail.
## 7. Metrics and statistical plan

Primary quality metrics are task/rubric completion, decision-regression rate,
unsupported-decision rate, evidence-grounded answer accuracy, and useful-change
rate. The last metric is mandatory: a system that refuses every change is not a
successful provenance system.

Trust and safety metrics are authority-laundering rate, provenance-faithfulness,
correct abstention under missing evidence, tamper/drift detection, and false
block rate on benign or correctly updated decisions.

Efficiency metrics are input/output tokens, wall-clock latency, model/tool calls,
history-search operations, and cost per successfully completed rubric item.

Use paired instances and shared seeds across arms. Analyze binary outcomes with
paired tests or mixed-effects logistic regression, treating task/project as a
cluster; report bootstrap confidence intervals for cost and latency. Pre-register
the primary outcome, exclusion gates, prompt templates, stopping rules, and the
distinction between exploratory and confirmatory analyses.
## 8. Confounds and validity gates
- Give all arms the complete task environment. The earlier single-file Hindcast
probe caused the baseline to refuse because it could not inspect the repo.
- Use neutral task wording. Terms such as “restore” and “add back” reveal that a
direction was previously removed.
- Screen for benchmark contamination and memorized public projects; use recent,
partner-held, or procedurally generated cases where possible.
- Keep information and authority separate. A fluent rationale is not automatically
an accepted rationale, and a cited source is not automatically true.
- Score both preservation and justified reversal. Avoid building a benchmark in
which “never deviate from history” is always correct.
- Blind artifact-quality graders to the experimental arm. Use execution/rubric
checks where available and human review for decision-level ambiguity.
- Report transport and trust-root assumptions explicitly. A stripped capsule is
an ordinary artifact; self-asserted attribution is not signed identity.
## 9. Pilot implementation

The smallest credible partner pilot uses 6–10 ARA/PaperBench research projects,
with one Continue task and one Audit or Counterfactual task per project. Run the
four essential arms (final artifact, raw history, Proofpress, Proofpress
ablation) with 3–5 shared seeds. Add ordinary memory after the harness is stable.
Implementation sequence:
1. Select projects with at least one material accepted decision, one rejected or
failed route, and executable or rubric-grounded outcomes.
2. Freeze a gold decision sheet containing source, status, rationale, evidence,
expiry/scope, and conditions under which reversal is correct.
3. Build deterministic package generation for every arm from the same source
record; do not hand-author a better Proofpress prompt.
4. Split each original trajectory at realistic handoff boundaries and run fresh
agents in isolated workspaces with equal repository/resource access.
5. Record tokens, latency, tool calls, artifact versions, claims, and evaluator
outputs in a machine-readable run ledger.
6. Run a gate pilot first: confirm the baseline sometimes fails, benign tasks
remain achievable, and graders agree before scaling.
7. Scale only after the task/material gate passes; publish prompts, schemas,
rubrics, aggregate results, and sanitized traces where licenses permit.
## 10. Product implications if the hypothesis holds

The research should guide product iteration, not merely produce a leaderboard.
Likely protocol additions to explore are typed `source_class`, explicit
`decision_status`, scoped `evidence_ref`, and supersession/expiry semantics.
These must preserve the current distinction between computed facts and attributed
testimony; they are research candidates, not implementation commitments.
The strongest defensible product line would be:

> Memory helps agents continue. Proofpress gives the artifact a shared,
> checkable past—so continuity does not silently launder trust.
